title: Rebuilding Emotional Safety at Home
learningGoal: Strengthen emotional safety for both caregiver and child after DFV.
microLesson: Emotional safety grows through predictability, calm tone, and consistent responses. Children need reassurance that home is stable and safe.
activity: List three ways you can increase emotional safety this week.

title: Understanding Children’s Stress Signals
learningGoal: Identify early signs of stress in children and respond supportively.
microLesson: Stress signals include clinginess, withdrawal, irritability, sleep issues, or regression. Early recognition prevents escalation.
activity: Complete a stress‑signal observation for your child.

title: Repairing Trust After Conflict
learningGoal: Learn how to repair trust with children after stressful events.
microLesson: Repair involves acknowledging feelings, offering reassurance, and reconnecting through calm presence and predictable routines.
activity: Complete a 10‑minute repair conversation using the provided script.

title: Strengthening Parenting Confidence
learningGoal: Build confidence in your parenting skills after DFV disruption.
microLesson: Confidence grows through small successes, predictable routines, and recognising your strengths as a caregiver.
activity: Identify three parenting strengths and one area you want to grow.

title: Creating Calm Spaces
learningGoal: Design a calming space at home to support emotional regulation.
microLesson: Calm spaces reduce overwhelm and help children regulate. They can include soft items, quiet corners, or sensory tools.
activity: Create or plan a calming space and describe its features.

title: Managing Caregiver Stress
learningGoal: Learn strategies to manage your own stress to support family stability.
microLesson: Caregiver stress affects children’s behaviour. Techniques include grounding, time‑outs, and seeking support.
activity: Write a short stress‑management plan for yourself.

title: Weekly Reflection and Progress Review
learningGoal: Reflect on progress and identify next steps for emotional safety.
microLesson: Reflection helps track improvements in routines, emotional safety, and parenting confidence.
activity: Write a 150‑word reflection on what improved and what still feels challenging.
